![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14190413/assets/ae57faa04abd053e4a58d751cc084d58e07e84e0520c99a33a122f58dfd8f18c.png)

A slice of jackfruit is placed in an air dryer. The graph of the moisture content $M(t)$, in percent, after $t$ hours is shown above. Approximate the rate of change of the moisture content at $t=3$ using a forward difference with step size $h=2.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint*: Assume that the rate of change is negative if the content decreases.

After $3$ hour, the rate of change of moisture content is {{field-1}} percent per hour.
question.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{M}^{′}(t)≈\frac{M(t+h)-M(t)}{h},
$$

at the time $t=3$ with step size $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}^{′}(3) & ≈\frac{M(3+2)-M(3)}{2} \\  & =\frac{M(5)-M(3)}{2} \\  & =\frac{20-40}{2} \\  & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$

So, after $3$ hour, the rate of change of moisture content is $-10$ percent per hour.
